skill.name: stitch-design
skill.description: Unified Stitch design workflow for enhancing UI prompts, synthesizing design systems, and generating or editing high-fidelity screens with Stitch MCP.
skill.summary: Create consistent Stitch UI designs from structured prompts and project design system context.
skill.author: google-labs-code

security_audit.summary: The static findings are false positives caused by Markdown code spans, relative documentation links, and UI design terminology. One semantic risk remains: the workflow encourages automatic download of Stitch-generated HTML and screenshots into the workspace. Gate downloads with user confirmation, URL validation, and filename sanitization.

remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user confirmation before downloading outputComponents assets, and allow only expected Stitch-generated URLs.

remediation.issue: Downloaded file naming is not constrained
remediation.suggestion: Sanitize generated filenames to a basename under .stitch/designs and reject path separators or parent directory segments.
Prefer a safe download helper with size limits, content-type checks, and overwrite prompts instead of direct curl commands.

content.value_statement: Teams often start Stitch work with vague UI requests and inconsistent design language. This skill turns those ideas into structured prompts, design systems, and downloadable design assets.
actual_capabilities: Enhances rough UI requests with professional design terminology and page structure.
Routes design requests to text generation, screen editing, or design system workflows.
Uses Stitch MCP tool schemas for project lookup, screen generation, and screen editing.
Incorporates existing .stitch/DESIGN.md tokens when creating new screen prompts.
Synthesizes project design rules into a .stitch/DESIGN.md source file.
Guides download of generated HTML and screenshots into .stitch/designs.
limitations: Requires a configured Stitch MCP server and access to the target project.
Does not implement production frontend code from the generated design.
Generated HTML and screenshots should be reviewed before use.
Project lookup and asset downloads need care in sensitive workspaces.

use_cases.title: Create a Product Landing Page
use_cases.description: Turn a short product idea into a structured Stitch prompt and generated screen.

use_cases.title: Standardize Design Language
use_cases.description: Analyze representative Stitch screens and document reusable color, typography, spacing, and component rules.

use_cases.title: Refine Existing Screens
use_cases.description: Make targeted visual changes to an existing Stitch screen while preserving the established layout.

prompt_templates.title: Generate One Screen
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a new design.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use stitch-design to turn this idea into a Stitch prompt and generate one desktop screen: [describe product, audience, and goal].

prompt_templates.title: Edit a Screen
prompt_templates.scenario: Focused improvement to an existing design.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use stitch-design to edit screen [screen name or ID]. Keep the layout, but improve [component], [color], and [spacing].

prompt_templates.title: Create a Design System
prompt_templates.scenario: Document design rules from existing Stitch work.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use stitch-design to analyze project [projectId] and create .stitch/DESIGN.md from screens [screen names]. Include colors, typography, layout, and component rules.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Coherent Flow
prompt_templates.prompt: Use stitch-design to plan and generate a coherent [web or mobile] flow for [task]. Reuse .stitch/DESIGN.md, propose screen order, then refine each screen.

output_examples.input: A founder asks for a premium onboarding landing page.
output: An enhanced Stitch prompt with audience, structure, palette, and interaction guidance.
A generated screen summary with suggestions returned from Stitch.

output_examples.input: A design lead needs consistent future screens for an existing project.
output_examples.output: A concise design system document covering atmosphere, colors, typography, components, and layout principles.

output_examples.input: A designer wants a dashboard screen polished without changing the layout.
output: A targeted edit prompt that names the component, visual change, and expected result.
Updated local design assets after approval and review.

best_practices: Provide projectId, device type, audience, and page goal before generation.
Review .stitch/DESIGN.md before creating or editing screens.
Approve downloaded assets and inspect generated HTML before reuse.
anti_patterns: Using vague prompts such as make it nice without layout or audience details.
Regenerating an entire screen when a focused edit would preserve consistency.
Downloading generated assets into a project without confirming source and filename.

faq.question: What does this skill create?
faq.answer: It creates enhanced Stitch prompts, generated or edited design screens, and project design system documentation.

faq.question: Does it require Stitch MCP?
faq.answer: Yes. The workflows depend on Stitch MCP tools for project lookup, screen generation, editing, and asset access.

faq.question: Can it work with an existing design system?
faq.answer: Yes. It checks .stitch/DESIGN.md and uses existing tokens when shaping new prompts.

faq.question: Does it write production application code?
faq.answer: No. It focuses on design prompts, Stitch screens, screenshots, HTML assets, and design documentation.

faq.question: How should teams handle downloaded assets?
faq.answer: Teams should confirm the source, sanitize filenames, and review generated HTML before placing assets in a project.

faq.question: Which assistants can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
